claims.statement: In the specified 1,836-encoding labeled Prüfer sample of orders 8 through 16, there are 37 eligible parameter rows; all have p=x+2, select every original leaf, have S<0, and satisfy E<=(x+1)Q. No sampled eligible row has a proper favorable-leaf selector.
claims.scope: Only the seeded, shape-biased labeled Prüfer sample and exact arithmetic protocol in the C4-F1 report and evidence. Bounded evidence only; no universal conclusion about ordinary trees.
claims.reason: retained: scratch replay reproduces the finite sample totals, and an independent induced-forest polynomial recurrence plus literal subset counts reconstruct every eligible graph, original leaf selector, per-tag summand, full S, and E=kU+C count. These checks support the bounded statement only; the sample is not exhaustive and does not prove or refute the universal aggregate or CT_x inequality.

limitations: The source computation samples labeled trees at orders 8 through 16 and is not exhaustive at any searched order.
No proper favorable-leaf selector occurred in this sampled eligible population; this does not establish that proper selectors are impossible.
Every eligible sample row has p=x+2, so the run does not separate CT_x from the current-rank addability budget.
All sampled full aggregates are negative; these finite cases provide neither a proof nor a counterexample to the universal lower-region aggregate.
